threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the buses run on time. The only thing more unreliable than them is the weather forecast!
Last night on the 59, a bloke serenaded the whole bus with an off-key rendition of ‘Wonderwall’—everyone pretended to ignore him, but we were all chuckling.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I found a stray cat curled up on the windowsill, soaking in the sun like it owned the place. That's when it felt like home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg do you find spontaneous techno parties in the middle of the street after a BVG strike. It's like our own version of street carnaval.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by how they instinctively know to walk around the BART delays and find shortcuts through alleys you wouldn’t normally notice.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni bus today that had a guy in a full suit trying to do a juggling act with coffee and a phone, while it stopped every two blocks. Classic San Francisco chaos.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all fancy bar terraces; they miss the old ladies arguing over who's got the best pilates class in the park.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell they're new if they still think La Fira de Gràcia is just a one-day event; locals know it’s a month-long street party.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look confused when the bus driver yells 'next stop!' instead of just saying it. Locals just nod and hold on tight.
Last night on the 133, a guy started singing 'No Woman, No Cry' loudly, and by the end, half the bus was clapping along like it was a concert.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The first time I saw a guy in shorts waiting for a bus while it snowed. That’s when I knew I was really home in Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin do you find a club that opens at 6 AM, celebrates daytime raves, and serves genuine Döner to the sleep-deprived.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by their quick sidestep when a BART delay announcement interrupts their flow. Tourists just stand there, looking helpless.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy playing violin at Mission & 24th, Muni bus honked, and he played off the rhythm like it was part of the show. Classic SF magic.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think they can just stroll into a bar and expect to chat for hours. In Gràcia, it’s more about a quick caña and moving on.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They’re the ones trying to order a ‘café con leche’ before 10am, still unaware it's ‘café amb llet’ here in Gràcia.
